cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD, friends! The psalmist asks the question in verse 1, then answers it right away: "My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth." (Psalm 121:2) No long pause, no guessing game. When the song asks where help comes from, the answer is already waiting.

The answer is slip, friends! The psalm says, "He will not allow your foot to slip…" (Psalm 121:3) Slipping is that sudden stumble that makes your stomach drop. I've done it on a floor dusted with flour, and my mustache went flying one way while the rest of me went the other. The psalm says the LORD won't allow it.

The answer is False, friends. The psalm says, "your Protector will not slumber." (Psalm 121:3) Then it comes back and says, "Behold, the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor sleep." (Psalm 121:4) It's not a nap here and there. The Protector doesn't slumber or sleep, period.

The answer is sun, friends! "The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night." (Psalm 121:6) Shade is exactly what you want when the sun is beating down. And the psalm just said the LORD is the shade on your right hand (Psalm 121:5). That's the picture.

The answer is False, friends. The psalm says, "The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night." (Psalm 121:6) It names the day and then it names the night. When the sun goes down, the psalm keeps going.
The answer is True, friends! The psalm says, "The LORD will guard you from all evil…" (Psalm 121:7) Look at that word all. The psalm doesn't pick and choose. It says all evil.

The answer is soul, friends! "He will preserve your soul." (Psalm 121:7) It's right there after the line about guarding you from all evil. The verse names your soul, and the LORD is the One who preserves it. Nothing else fills that blank.

The answer is for all time, friends! The psalm says the LORD will watch over your coming and going, "…both now and forevermore." (Psalm 121:8) Now and forevermore. It's the last line of the song, and it doesn't have an end date.
